name: Tokyo Metro + Toei subway
price_note: ¥180-¥330 per ride (distance-based). 24/48/72-hour Tokyo Subway Ticket: ¥800/¥1,200/¥1,500 for tourists.
pros: Dense network covering every central neighborhood
Trains every 2-5 minutes at rush, 5-10 minutes off-peak
Station signs and announcements in English, Chinese, Korean
cons: Transfers between Tokyo Metro and Toei usually cost extra unless you hold the combined pass

name: JR East lines (Yamanote, Chuo, Sobu)
price_note: ¥150-¥320 per ride. The Yamanote loop is the tourist backbone — one full loop takes ~60 minutes.
pros: Runs to most major districts (Shinjuku, Shibuya, Ueno, Tokyo, Akihabara)
More frequent and longer-running hours than the subway
Connects directly to Shinkansen and airport express trains
cons: Fares stack separately from subway unless transferring through a single IC tap

name: Taxi
price_note: ¥500 base for first 1.096 km, then ¥100 per 255 m. 22:00-05:00 surcharge of +20%. Short cross-district rides ¥1,000-¥2,500.
pros: Drivers are licensed, meter-only, polite; rear doors open automatically
Apps (GO, S.RIDE, DiDi) work well and accept cards
cons: Traffic is heavy around Shibuya/Shinjuku on weekends

name: City bus (Toei Bus)
price_note: Flat ¥210 adult / ¥110 child in central Tokyo.
pros: Reaches areas the subway misses (inner Roppongi, waterfront)
Pay-on-entry is simple with IC card tap
cons: Slower than the subway and less English signage

name: Bike share (HELLO CYCLING / docomo)
pros: Fun for riverside or park routes (Arakawa, Sumida, Imperial Palace)
Docking stations at most convenience stores and many hotels
cons: Riding on sidewalks is technically restricted; busy areas are stressful
Helmets are recommended but often not provided

name: On foot
pros: Central Tokyo is dense and walkable — neighborhoods unfold best on foot
Sidewalks, crossings, and signage are excellent
cons: Summer heat (July-August) and humidity can be brutal — plan rest stops
